summaryForNext: Assessed UAR (dce44e78) against codex-rs (986ff1cc) and a 14-harness survey on harness assembly, prompts, skill activation and use, MCP, tools, context, subagents, resiliency, extensions, observability, testing, and UI protocols. Twelve of thirteen supplied-analysis claims verified; one FALSE (registries merge early and freeze, so the fix is per-step re-projection) and one PARTIAL (jsonschema caret-pinned, not in versions.toml, unused on tool path). Immediate-value gaps: context correctness (severable tool pairs, trimmable system prompt, unbounded tool output), fail-closed tool arguments and effect classification, deterministic prompt ordering for caching, budgeted skill catalog with explicit activation and max_active, unread resilience knobs and health gating. Structural: typed turn/step assembly, projected MCP runtime with real stdio sandbox, thread-native subagents, project-instruction and world-state injection, MCP Apps. Open questions for analyze: build-vs-adopt for fragment/world-state types and jsonschema validation; whether a guardian-style model reviewer belongs behind Cedar; A2UI v1.0 timing. Adversarial review WARNINGs carried: survey claims are primary-source but not pipeline-scored, re-fetch before promoting any to a change; the phase goal's ordered spec-scoped plan is owed by the plan stage; Codex citations could not be packet-verified because the workspace is external.
